newsitem.title: UK: Pakistan president dismisses Bhutto government - BBC.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president dismisses Bhutto government - BBC.

text.p: Pakistant President Farooq Leghari has dismissed the government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, according to BBC radio, citing its local correspondent.
The BBC also reported on Monday that the army was reported to have sealed all the country's airports.

"President Farooq Ahmed Leghari has dissolved National Assembly with immediate effect and the Prime Minister and her Cabinet will cease to hold office forthwith, it was announced today," the news agency said.

The local BBC correspondent said Bhutto was in the prime minister's official residence in Islamabad. "There are troops outside the house," he said, adding that she was "not officially under detention".
Troops were also outside television and radio stations, the BBC reporter said.
In response to a question, he said it did not feel like a military coup was taking place, more like a "kind of a constitutional coup".

He said the president had dissolved the national assembly and had already set Feburary 3 as the date for a fresh general election. A caretaker prime minister had been appointed, the reporter said, without naming the person.
